roastFacts.text: SpaceX bills Falcon 9 as the world's first orbital-class reusable rocket.
On January 24, 2021, a Falcon 9 set the record for most satellites launched by a single rocket: 143.
Individual Falcon 9 boosters have flown as many as 37 times.
SpaceX says Falcon Heavy's liftoff thrust equals approximately eighteen 747 aircraft at full power.
SpaceX says Falcon Heavy can lift the equivalent of a fully loaded 737 jetliner, complete with passengers.
Its first payload was Elon Musk's personal Tesla Roadster, with a mannequin named "Starman" at the wheel.
Fully fueled, the Saturn V weighed about as much as 400 elephants.
NASA says its launch thrust created more power than 85 Hoover Dams.
The fuel for one lunar mission could drive a 30-mpg car around the world about 800 times.

name: Starship (Super Heavy + Starship, V3)

roastFacts.text: SpaceX calls Starship the world's most powerful launch vehicle ever developed.
The Super Heavy booster lands by being caught by a pair of hydraulic arms on the launch tower.
After several setbacks, Starship did not reach orbit until its fourteenth flight test.
NASA says SLS produces 15% more maximum thrust than the Saturn V.
At 322 ft, SLS Block 1 is taller than the Statue of Liberty.
The whole 5.75-million-lb rocket rests on the aft skirts of its two boosters.
All four N1 launch attempts, from 1969 to 1972, failed.
Its first stage clustered thirty NK-15 engines, managed by an analog computer (KORD) that shut down the engine opposite any that failed.
The second flight caused one of the largest conventional explosions ever and put its launch pad out of action for 18 months.
The main engines burned fuel fast enough to drain an average family swimming pool in under 25 seconds.
The external tank was the only part of the Shuttle that was not reused.
Two orbiters were lost in accidents, Challenger in 1986 and Columbia in 2003, killing 14 astronauts in total.
An Atlas V 551 launched New Horizons toward Pluto on January 19, 2006.
Its first stage runs on a single Russian-made RD-180 engine.
ULA says Atlas V builds on a heritage of more than 600 Atlas program launches.
Its hydrogen-fuelled ignition often produced a large fireball that scorched the outside of the boosters.
It sent the Parker Solar Probe to study the Sun's atmosphere.
The Delta family's six-decade run ended at 389 launches.
The first Ariane 5 ECA launch (11 December 2002) ended in failure: it veered off course and was destroyed about three minutes into flight.
An Ariane 5 (flight VA256) launched the James Webb Space Telescope on 25 December 2021.
Ariane 5 had a run of 82 consecutive successful launches between 2003 and 2017.
ESA says a fully loaded Ariane 6 weighs roughly as much as one and a half Airbus A380s.
Its 8,200-tonne mobile gantry is nearly a thousand tonnes heavier than the Eiffel Tower.
On the maiden flight, VA262, the satellites reached orbit but the Vinci engine failed to ignite a third time to deorbit the upper stage.
On its second flight a solid booster's nozzle fell off about 37 seconds in, and Vulcan still reached its planned orbit.
Its first launch carried the Peregrine lunar lander.

name: New Glenn (7x2)

roastFacts.text: It is named after John Glenn, the first American to orbit Earth.
The booster first landed successfully on the second flight, NG-2, on November 13, 2025.
In May 2026 a New Glenn exploded during preparations for an Amazon Leo launch, heavily damaging LC-36.

roastFacts.text: Soyuz-2 is the seventh major iteration of the Soyuz family and still flies from pads built for its R-7 ancestors.
In 2015 it emerged that parts of the Vostochny assembly complex had been designed for a different rocket variant and were too small for Soyuz-2.
The July 2013 failure was traced to three yaw-rate sensors installed in the wrong orientation.
In December 2010 an upper stage overloaded with 1,500 kg of liquid oxygen failed to reach orbital velocity, losing three GLONASS satellites.
Its nickname is "Pang-Wu" ("Fat-Five").
The first 5B's core stage may have been the most massive object to make an uncontrolled re-entry since Salyut 7 (1991) and Skylab (1979).
It launched all three modules of the Tiangong space station.
The H3 maiden flight in March 2023 failed when the second-stage engine did not ignite.
JAXA says the H3's LE-9 engine needed more thrust than any liquid rocket engine Japan had ever developed.
Its Rutherford engines are the first electric-pump-fed engines to power an orbital-class rocket, with the pumps running on lithium-polymer batteries.
The second stage hot-swaps its batteries and throws away the empty ones to save mass.
Almost all of the engine parts are 3D printed.
In 1973 Saturn IBs carried three crews to Skylab, and in 1975 one launched the Apollo side of the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project.
A backup Saturn IB was readied for a Skylab rescue mission but never flew.
On its first flight the rocket worked perfectly, but the Polyus payload fired its engines the wrong way and fell into the ocean.
Its second and last flight carried the uncrewed Buran shuttle, which landed automatically after two orbits.
Mothballed Energia and Buran hardware at Baikonur was destroyed when the assembly building roof collapsed.
